solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I walk about on cold frozen area

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: about means the word for walk is turned round

parts.note: to pace is to walk

explanation.surface: Someone describes strolling around on a chilly frozen stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walk about' looks like strolling around, but 'about' turns the walking word backwards; in an across answer 'on' means after.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar cap of permanent ice is a frozen expanse covering a region.

clue.text: Copper leads a training session with a Spanish team

indicators.note: leads means the copper symbol goes in front of the rest

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a drill is a training exercise

explanation.surface: A policeman runs a training session with a team from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuadrilla is a matador's support crew of picadors and banderilleros in a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: King Charles admitted wearing something regal

parts.note: CR, Carolus Rex, is the royal cipher of King Charles
to own up is to admit, so owned means admitted

explanation.surface: King Charles confessed to wearing royal regalia.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowned monarch is one wearing a crown, the most regal of headwear.

clue.text: Pastry confection that is soft on top

indicators.note: on top means the soft letter sits above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A pastry dessert whose topping is soft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on top' puts P above IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a dish baked in pastry, sweet or savoury.

clue.text: Cheese pie dished up with corn, nothing more

indicators.note: food dished up is served out in a new arrangement, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A meal of cheese, a pie and some corn, and nothing else on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished up' scrambles PIE and CORN into PECORIN; 'more' adds O on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a hard Italian cheese made from ewe's milk.

clue.text: Iron stuff in cupboard

definitions.meaning: to iron clothes is to smooth them flat
to cram or squeeze something in tightly
an old or Scottish word for a cupboard or large wardrobe

explanation.surface: An instruction to iron the things kept in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, one after another: smooth flat, cram in, and a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means smoothing clothes, squeezing something in, and, in older or Scottish use, a cupboard.

clue.text: What follows first of carriages on train?

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word carriages

parts.note: a train of events is a sequence

explanation.surface: A railway puzzle: what comes after the first carriage on a train?
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is not the railway but a train of thought or events: a SEQUENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence is a result, the outcome that follows from an action.

clue.text: Coffee mugs filled with last of cointreau? Cheers!

indicators.note: filled with means the robbing word holds the picked letter inside

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word cointreau

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

explanation.surface: Mugs of coffee laced with a splash of Cointreau: cheers!
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' looks like cups but is the verb meaning steals from; 'filled with' puts the U inside. 'Cheers' is everyday British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Robusta is a hardy species of coffee bean, stronger and more bitter than arabica.

clue.text: Either way, it's unacceptable

definitions.note: not allowed or out of order, as in saying that behaviour simply won't do

indicators.note: either way says the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: not allowed or out of order, as in saying that behaviour simply won't do

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, it simply won't do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either way' sounds like 'regardless' but says the answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, as in 'that's just not on', means something is not permissible.

clue.text: African yak, I see, finally extinct

parts.note: to yak is to chatter, or gab
I, the Roman numeral, is one

indicators.note: the final letter of the word see dies out, leaving it one letter short

explanation.surface: A news item: an African yak, it seems, has at last gone extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yak' looks like the animal but is the verb to chatter. 'finally extinct' drops the last E of SEE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Gabon, a West African country, is Gabonese.

clue.text: Vineyard owner on way back hurries at first to bar

indicators.note: travelling the way back means the letters run in reverse order
at first points to the opening letter of the word hurries

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A wine grower, heading home, rushes off to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: H (hurries at first) plus TO plus BAN gives HTOBAN, which 'on way back' reverses. 'bar' looks like a pub but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible (1 Kings 21) Naboth owned the vineyard that King Ahab coveted and Jezebel seized.

clue.text: One with specific rights is stopping ambassador entering European country

indicators.note: entering means the combined piece goes inside the country's name

parts.note: France is a country of Europe

indicators.note: is stopping means IS plugs the gap inside the ambassador's title

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone with special rights is barring an ambassador from coming into a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' plugs IS inside the ambassador's title, and 'entering' puts that whole piece inside the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchisee is granted a licence to trade under another company's brand within agreed terms.

clue.text: Musical artist and I perform song: scary!

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s hippie rock musical
RA, Royal Academician, is crossword shorthand for an artist
to sing is to perform a song

explanation.surface: A musical performer and I sing a terrifying song together.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, stands for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightening enough to make your hair stand on end is terrifying.

clue.text: Writer's article appearing in Standard, devoid of substance

indicators.note: appearing in means the article goes inside the remaining letters
with its substance gone, the word Standard keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer's piece in the Evening Standard is criticised as lacking any substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of substance' empties STANDARD to SD; 'appearing in' puts AN between them. The Standard is a London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin.

clue.text: Joyful leading lady's part

indicators.note: part says a piece of the words leading lady's is taken, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: The star actress is happy with her role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a theatrical role but signals letters taken from inside 'leading lady's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and joyful are both words for being happy.

clue.text: One rejected university study, along with guy unsuited to academia?

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is one

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a den is a private study
a guy is a rope or cable steadying a tent or mast

explanation.surface: Someone turned down by a university and its study course, along with a man, is not cut out for academic life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the university letter and the study word round together. 'guy' is not a man but a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be educated is unsuited to academic study, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Writer excising chapter one first of all

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An author cuts the opening chapter, chapter one, before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excising' looks like a deletion signal, but 'first of all' takes the initials of 'excising chapter one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco was the Italian novelist of The Name of the Rose.

clue.text: Sweet, shortened version of French organ work after Rossini intro

indicators.note: after says the musical work comes behind the Rossini letter
a shortened version loses its final letter

parts.note: Le Monde is a French newspaper, and a newspaper is an organ

indicators.note: intro means the opening letter of the name Rossini

parts.note: op, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A sweet short arrangement of a French organ piece, following a Rossini overture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' is a newspaper, not the instrument; 'shortened version of' drops its last letter, and 'after' sends the work behind R.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon drop is a boiled sweet flavoured with lemon.

clue.text: Mountain, terrible threat in early part of day

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters sit within the word for morning

parts.note: the morn is the morning, the early part of the day

indicators.note: terrible says the word threat is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A mountain poses a terrible danger in the early hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' looks like a description of the danger but scrambles the letters, and 'in' places them within the morning word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Matterhorn is a famous Alpine peak on the Swiss-Italian border.

clue.text: Less sober Greek character brought into line

indicators.note: brought into means the Greek letter goes inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A drunker Greek man is made to toe the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person but is the letter PSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly drunk, so the comparative means more drunk, not as sober.

clue.text: Uniform Salvation Army made without padding

indicators.note: with its padding removed the word made keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army uniform was made with no padding in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like a noun for the Army's clothes but is an adjective. 'without padding' strips MADE to ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uniform is identical throughout, alike or the same in every part.

clue.text: One who'll eat and drink, briefly entertained by sister

indicators.note: entertained by means the clipped drink is held inside the sister's abbreviation
briefly means the drink's word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: coffee is a drink

explanation.surface: A guest who eats and drinks is hosted by a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eat and drink' looks like one phrase, but only 'eat' defines; 'briefly' clips the drink and 'entertained by' sets it inside the sister's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, so a scoffer is a greedy eater.

clue.text: Boisterously play piano coming to end of concert

indicators.note: coming to the end means the piano letter moves to the back of the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A pianist bangs out a lively piece as the concert closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to end of' moves the P of PROM to the back. The Proms are a famous London summer concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to play roughly and energetically, like children frolicking.

clue.text: Gets started? Writer might not, having this

definitions.meaning: begins, as a show or shop does
read as nought plus pens, no pens: an author with none might not get going

explanation.walkthrough: The second part splits the answer as O PENS, zero pens, a reason a writer might fail to start.
explanation.definitionFit: When something begins or commences, it is said to open, as a play does.

clue.text: My freedom's under threat, for sure

definitions.meaning: read literally, a person saying they will be tied up, about to lose their liberty
an old-fashioned way of saying I am certain, I guarantee it

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: I will be tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a dated idiom of certainty, while literally it means being tied up and losing liberty.

clue.text: Handle dog well, but only intermittently

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador dog

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter of the word well

explanation.surface: Advice to manage a dog properly, if only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb about the dog, but is a noun: a name. 'but only intermittently' takes EL from WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or title, which is what a label gives something.

clue.text: Italian family by the sea here in Cannes

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
ici is French for here, and Cannes is in France

explanation.surface: An Italian family is staying by the sea here at Cannes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Cannes' signals a French word: ICI for here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the powerful banking dynasty who ruled Renaissance Florence.

clue.text: Publicity supporting Democrat backing British city

indicators.note: backing means the other pieces come behind, after the British abbreviation

parts.note: an ad is publicity for a product
to be for something is to support it
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: Political publicity backing a Democrat, with British support, in campaign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' puts the other pieces behind the British abbreviation. Bradford is a city in West Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a large industrial city in northern England.

clue.text: Cockney's own greeting

definitions.meaning: a Cockney drops the h, so the verb meaning to possess is said without it
a Latin salutation, hail, as in the prayer to Mary

explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop initial H, so 'have' (own) is said as 'ave.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is Latin for hail, a formal salutation, while the dropped-h form means possess.

clue.text: Briefly leaving the straight and narrow, girl finds joint

indicators.note: briefly means the phrase's word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to stray from the straight and narrow is to go astray
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl who strays from the moral path discovers a seedy dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' clips the Y from ASTRAY. 'joint' looks like a dive but is the anatomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The astragalus, or ankle bone, forms the ankle joint; astragal is an old name for it.

clue.text: Overjoyed gun owners checked in record time

indicators.note: checked in means the gun owners are booked inside the record, as at a hotel

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
the NRA is the National Rifle Association, the US gun owners' lobby

explanation.surface: Gun owners are delighted to have checked in in record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checked in' puts the gun lobby inside the record. 'record' looks like the adjective in 'record time' but is a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrapt is a rare variant of enraptured, meaning carried away with delight.
